description: The Transportation Secure Data Center gives access to detailed transportation data from travel surveys and studies carried out across the United States. It holds GPS readings for millions of miles of travel, with vehicle characteristics and demographics of survey participants. NREL screens the data for quality, translates each dataset into a consistent format and prepares it for spatial analysis, adding vehicle fuel economy and road grade and joining points to the road network. Coverage is national, made up of regional surveys. Access is described as free; the record in the DOE Open Energy Data Initiative links to the TSDC portal and offers a sample of the California Household Travel Survey as a zip file. Caveats: the NREL portal could not be read on 2026-09-26, so the access terms for the detailed GPS data are not given here, and the related paper describes the centre as a way to open GPS data while preserving participant privacy, so users should check the portal's terms before planning work. The data support calibration of travel demand and agent-based traffic models, energy and fuel use studies and route choice analysis. They complement the National Travel Survey data and the FRISM freight model catalogued here.
